concepts.def: A force, or a system of forces, may cause an object to rotate instead of simply moving along a straight line. Rotation happens when the line of action of the force misses the fixed point about which the object can turn, so that the force acts at some perpendicular distance from that point.

The fixed point about which an object turns. A moment is always stated about a particular pivot: the same force can have a large moment about one pivot and no moment at all about another, because the perpendicular distance differs in each case.

The turning effect of a force is called the moment of the force. It measures how strongly a force tends to turn an object about a pivot, and it depends on both the size of the force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot.

The size of the moment is defined by the equation moment of a force = force × distance, written in symbols as M = F d. The two quantities multiply, so doubling either the force or the distance doubles the moment.

concepts.term: Quantities and units in M = F d
concepts.def: Moment of a force, M, is in newton-metres, Nm. Force, F, is in newtons, N. Distance, d, is in metres, m. A mass given in kilograms must first be converted to a weight in newtons, and a distance given in centimetres or millimetres must be converted to metres, before the equation is used.

In M = F d the distance d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force, in metres. It is not necessarily the length of the object, nor the distance measured along the object to the point where the force is applied; when the force acts at an angle to the object the perpendicular distance is shorter than that.

concepts.term: Line of action of a force
concepts.def: The straight line drawn through the point at which a force acts, along the direction of the force and extended in both directions. The distance d is measured from the pivot at right angles to this line. If the line of action passes through the pivot, d is zero and the moment is zero.

Every force acting on an object turns it about the pivot in one of two senses. A moment that would turn the object clockwise is called a clockwise moment; one that would turn it the other way is an anticlockwise moment. Moments acting in the same sense are added together.

If an object is balanced, the total clockwise moment about a pivot equals the total anticlockwise moment about that pivot. It is the moments that must match, not the forces and not the distances, so a small force far from the pivot can balance a large force close to it.

concepts.term: Finding an unknown force or distance
concepts.def: For a balanced object, writing total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment gives one equation that can be solved for a single unknown. To find a force, divide the known moment by that force's distance; to find a distance, divide the known moment by that force.

A rigid bar that turns about a pivot. A force applied at a large distance from the pivot produces a large moment, which is transmitted through the bar and can move a much larger load acting close to the pivot. The lever transmits the rotational effect of the force; it does not create energy.

Two or more toothed wheels meshed together. The teeth of one wheel push on the teeth of the next, transmitting the rotational effect from one wheel to the other. Meshed gears turn in opposite senses, and a larger driven gear turns more slowly than the smaller driving gear but with a larger moment.

concepts.term: Everyday examples of forces causing rotation
concepts.def: Pushing the edge of a door so that it swings on its hinges, pressing a bicycle pedal so that the crank turns about the axle, and pulling on a spanner so that a nut turns are all cases in which a force applied at a distance from a pivot causes rotation.

mcqs.q: A single steady force is applied to a gate that can swing freely on its hinges. In which case does the gate rotate?
options: When the line of action of the force does not pass through the hinges
Only when a second force acts on the gate at the same moment
Whenever the force is larger than the weight of the gate itself
Only when the force is applied exactly at the middle of the gate
mcqs.explain: A force acting at some perpendicular distance from the pivot has a moment about it, so it turns the gate.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of a force causing an object to rotate?
options: A crate being pulled along a level floor by a rope tied to it
Pushing on the edge of a revolving door to make it turn
Two people pushing a stalled car forwards along a flat road
A ball falling straight downwards after being dropped
mcqs.explain: The push acts at a distance from the central pivot, so it has a moment and the door rotates.

mcqs.q: A force acts on a bar that can turn about a pivot. What is the turning effect of that force called?
options: The rotational force of the bar at the pivot
The leverage of the force acting on the bar
The moment of the force about the pivot
The work done by the force on the bar
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the turning effect of a force is called the moment of the force.

mcqs.q: The size of the moment of a force is defined by which equation?
options: moment of a force = weight × distance
moment of a force = force × length of bar
moment of a force = force divided by distance
moment of a force = force × distance
mcqs.explain: This is the equation exactly as the specification gives it, written in symbols as M = F d.

mcqs.q: Which row gives the units to use in the equation M = F d?
options: M in newton-metres, F in grams, d in metres
M in newton-metres, F in newtons, d in metres
M in newtons, F in newtons, d in metres
M in joules, F in newtons, d in metres
mcqs.explain: These are the units the specification gives: Nm for the moment, N for the force and m for the distance.

mcqs.q: A 2.0 kg bag hangs from a beam at a perpendicular distance of 0.30 m from the pivot. The gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the moment of the bag's weight about the pivot?
options: 5.9 Nm
mcqs.explain: Weight = 2.0 x 9.8 = 19.6 N, so M = F d = 19.6 x 0.30 = 5.88 Nm, which is 5.9 Nm to two significant figures.

mcqs.q: In the equation M = F d, what exactly is the distance d?
options: The distance measured along the object from the pivot to where it acts
The distance the object moves in the direction of the force as it turns
The distance from one end of the object across to its far end
The perpendicular distance from the pivot to its line of action
mcqs.explain: This is the definition the specification gives, and it is measured in metres.

mcqs.q: A 60 N push is applied to a door along a line of action that passes exactly through the hinge. Why does the door not turn?
options: The perpendicular distance from the hinge is zero
The push is too small to overcome the weight of the door
A single force can never make a heavy object rotate
The push is applied too high up on the face of the door
mcqs.explain: With d = 0, M = F d gives a moment of zero however large the force is.

mcqs.q: A force of 25 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 15 cm from a pivot. What is the moment of the force about the pivot?
options: 375 Nm
mcqs.explain: 15 cm = 0.15 m, so M = F d = 25 x 0.15 = 3.75 Nm, with the distance in metres as the specification requires.

mcqs.q: A gardener prises up a stone using a long-handled spade as a lever. Why is a long handle better than a short one?
options: The longer handle increases the size of the push the gardener makes
The lever gives out more energy than the gardener puts into it
A longer handle is heavier, so it presses on the stone harder
The same push acts at a greater distance, so its moment is larger
mcqs.explain: M = F d, so increasing d while F stays the same increases the turning effect on the stone.

mcqs.q: An object is balanced about a pivot. Which statement must be true?
options: The total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment
The total of the forces on one side equals the total on the other side
Each force must act the same distance from the pivot as the other one
The pivot must be exactly at the middle of the whole object
mcqs.explain: This is the balanced condition exactly as the specification states it, about that same pivot.

mcqs.q: A plank balances on a pivot. A 10 N weight sits 0.60 m to the left of the pivot, and a 30 N weight sits somewhere to the right. What can be said about the 30 N weight?
options: It sits further from the pivot, because a larger force turns more
It sits closer to the pivot, because its force is the larger
It sits the same distance out, as the plank is balanced
It cannot balance, since the two forces are not equal
mcqs.explain: Equal moments with a larger force means a smaller distance: 0.20 m, one third of 0.60 m.

mcqs.q: A beam is balanced on a pivot. A 100 N weight hangs 0.75 m to the left of the pivot, and a single weight hangs 1.5 m to the right. What is that weight?
mcqs.explain: Anticlockwise moment = 100 x 0.75 = 75 Nm, so the unknown weight is 75 / 1.5 = 50 N.

mcqs.q: A rod is balanced on a pivot. A 6.0 N force acts 0.50 m from the pivot on one side, and an 8.0 N force acts on the other side. How far from the pivot is the 8.0 N force?
mcqs.explain: Clockwise moment = 6.0 x 0.50 = 3.0 Nm, so d = M / F = 3.0 / 8.0 = 0.375 m.

mcqs.q: What do a simple lever and a simple gear system have in common?
options: Both give out more energy than is put into them by the user
Both can be used to transmit the rotational effects of forces
Both increase the size of the force that you apply to them
Both change a force's direction without turning anything
mcqs.explain: This is what the specification says about them: each transmits the turning effect from one place to another.

mcqs.q: Two gear wheels are meshed together and the smaller one is driven clockwise. How does the larger gear turn?
options: Clockwise too, because the teeth push it the same way round
Anticlockwise but faster, because it is the bigger wheel
Anticlockwise, more slowly, and with a larger moment
Anticlockwise and slower, so its moment is smaller too
mcqs.explain: Meshed teeth reverse the sense; the larger wheel makes fewer turns per second and exerts a larger moment.
